paper: step 8. Provisional Section 3.3. The commons reference evaluation model is a trained artifact.
adr: Diagnostic checkpoint sweep after the register-coverage corpus amendment. Same taxonomy, gate rules, seed, and Qwen3 template. Training base is Qwen3-0.6B: the phone-deployment size. Two prior sweeps (0.6B then 1.7B) hit the same miss/over-fire wall on the narrow corpus. Size is not the lever. This run does not decide the published pin; it samples the loss curve on the widened corpus. The live pin is unchanged. After each checkpoint is merged, converted to GGUF Q8_0, and gated, the merged bf16 directory and that GGUF are deleted. Optimizer states are not kept on interval saves. Disk hygiene stays on. Run from /workspace.

base.note: Read at run time from the manifest. repoId here is a pin that must match. This is the training base for the register-coverage re-sweep. Do not change the live evaluator pin in this diagnostic. The 1.7B trainBaseRepoId stays for the unused within-family A/B recipe.

framework.whyNotUnsloth: 0.6B plus a few thousand short examples on an 80GB card does not need Unsloth's memory path. The standard stack is the one a reader can follow without a third training runtime.
framework.torch: supplied by the GPU image; not pinned here so a CUDA wheel is not overwritten

train.evalDatasetNote: The held-out suite is the final gate, never a training or hyperparameter split. The sweep gates after the fact. It does not train against the suite.

sweep.purpose: Register-coverage re-sweep on Qwen3-0.6B, the phone-deployment target. Same seed, dropout 0.1, LoRA rank 16, three epochs, a LoRA checkpoint every half epoch, Qwen3 template with generation spans. Corpus is the widened recipe (per-register formation slots, crude/imperative content, CSE contrastive pairs). Gate is the amended held-out suite. Disk hygiene stays on. Not a live-pin swap. Do not run until the review sample is accepted.
sweep.diskHygieneNote: At start, delete stale merged dirs and GGUFs under the artifacts tree. Interval saves are adapter-only (no optimizer states) and capped at minCheckpoints. After each checkpoint is merged, converted Q8_0, and gated, delete the merged bf16 directory and that GGUF before the next checkpoint. Keep the LoRA adapter and the gate report.

llamaCpp.note: convert_hf_to_gguf.py then llama-quantize Q8_0. The run records the resolved commit in checkpoints.json.

time.estimate: Training three epochs of 0.6B LoRA is tens of minutes on an 80GB card. Six merge-plus-Q8_0 exports and six held-out CPU gates dominate the wall time. Only one merged copy and one GGUF exist at a time. If the train loop itself is still running after 90 minutes, stop and report.
